::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Write-up in progress, from work at OxSTaR, University of Oxford, based at the
John Radcliffe Hospital.
:::

Clinical simulation training generates awkward data: courses, faculty,
candidates, equipment, feedback and outcomes, all related and all changing.
Delivery was largely for NHS staff, and reporting went to NHS stakeholders,
where it was used to account for how training spend translated into activity.

This project revisits that database design, rebuilt in SQL Server with
synthetic data. The rebuild demonstrates the data model and the reporting
rather than reproducing the original system.

What the write-up will cover:

- the data model, and why the entities were structured the way they were
- T-SQL scripts that build the schema and seed it with synthetic data, so the database runs from scratch
- the reporting queries the centre relied on, rewritten
- interface mockups showing how the system was used day to day, including Power BI dashbaords for interactive reports
- what changed operationally once the reporting existed, and what I would do differently now


[Paper (doi:10.1136/bmjstel-2019-000441)](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjstel-2019-000441)
